name: Gel

archived.reason: Gel Data Inc. shut down on 2 December 2025 and its team joined Vercel; Gel Cloud stopped taking new databases that day and closed on 31 January 2026. The code stays on GitHub under Apache 2.0 and can still be self-hosted, but nothing has been committed since December 2025.

summary: A “graph-relational” database, called EdgeDB until 2025, that runs on Postgres but gives it a typed object schema, automatic migrations and its own query language, EdgeQL, which compiles each query to one SQL statement.
intro: Gel is a server that sits in front of Postgres and owns it: it uses Postgres for storage and query execution, either a cluster it starts itself or an existing one named in `GEL_SERVER_BACKEND_DSN`. You describe data as object types in `.gel` files in a `dbschema` directory. Each object gets an immutable UUID, scalar fields are properties, and references to other objects are links, with `required` and `multi` setting cardinality, so there are no foreign keys or join tables to declare and no `NULL`: a missing value is an empty set. To change the schema you edit the files and run `gel migration create`; the server itself compares the new schema with the current one, asks you to confirm each change and writes a migration file that `gel migrate` applies, or `gel watch --migrate` applies changes as you save.

Queries are written in EdgeQL, where a query returns a nested shape of objects and their links, filtered and ordered, and every query compiles into a single SQL query instead of the many an ORM would send. Clients talk to it over its own binary protocol, with official libraries for TypeScript, Python, Go and Rust, or over HTTP and GraphQL; since Gel 6.0 in February 2025 it also accepts SQL, including inserts, updates and deletes through the Postgres wire protocol, and works with Drizzle. Built-in extensions add authentication (`ext::auth`, with email and password, OAuth, magic links and WebAuthn), embeddings from OpenAI, Mistral or Anthropic (`ext::ai`), and PostGIS; Gel 7.0 in November 2025 added role-based access control. That was the last major release: the company closed in December 2025, and the managed Gel Cloud shut down at the end of January 2026.
strengths: A typed schema with links and cardinality, and migrations generated by the database by comparing schemas, so schema changes are reviewed instead of hand-written
EdgeQL fetches deeply nested data without joins and always runs as one SQL query, avoiding the N+1 queries common with ORMs
It is still Postgres underneath, with SQL access since 6.0, so data can be reached by Postgres tools and migrated out
Authentication, access policies and embeddings built into the server, and `npx gel init` sets up a local instance in one step
limits: No longer maintained: the company has shut down, there is no managed service, and fixes and security updates have stopped
EdgeQL and the link-based model were, in the founders’ own words, unproven ideas that made Gel harder to learn
Another server between the application and Postgres, with its own protocol and query compiler, to run and size yourself
SQL access is partial: as of 6.0, window functions and recursive queries were not supported through the Postgres protocol

story: Yury Selivanov and Elvis Pranskevichus started MagicStack, a software consultancy, in 2008. For their own projects they built Caos, a “super ORM” with its own query language that was checked against a schema and compiled to SQL. By 2014 they concluded it could be a new kind of database, but only if it stopped being an ORM. Along the way they wrote PEP 492, which added `async`/`await` to Python, and released uvloop and the asyncpg Postgres driver.

A technical preview of EdgeDB was shown at PyCon in 2018, the first alpha came in April 2019, and EdgeDB Inc. was incorporated late that year. EdgeDB 1.0 shipped on 10 February 2022, after a long list of pre-releases, as “the first open source, graph-relational database”. In February 2025 the company renamed itself Gel, because “edge” suggested an edge-computing or graph database, and released Gel 6.0 with full SQL support.

On 2 December 2025 Gel Data Inc. announced it was shutting down and its team was joining Vercel to work on Python there. Gel Cloud closed on 31 January 2026. In their farewell the founders counted declarative schemas and the stateless protocol as good ideas, EdgeQL and the link model as unproven, and building on Postgres, which made Gel hard to tell apart from an ORM, as a questionable choice.

choices.choice: Build on Postgres instead of a new storage engine
choices.why: Postgres already had reliable storage, transactions and a query executor. The founders treated it as a foundation for a better database abstraction, and argued Gel was not an ORM because it had its own query language, type system, protocol and clients.
They wanted a formally defined language that “matches SQL in power and surpasses it in clarity and brevity”, composable without Cartesian explosions and able to return nested data in one query.

choices.choice: Objects and links instead of tables and foreign keys
choices.why: Giving every object an identity and making relationships first-class removed primary keys, foreign keys and join tables from the schema, and let the database generate migrations by comparing schemas.
